how_we_lost: P1 (Sauron) killed us on round 10 (turn 39) with Sauron and two Nazgûl. On round 9 our Toxic Deluge was meant to go off at X=5 and kill the Orc Army, Nazgûl and Sephiroth. It resolved at X=0 (Forge chooses X) and killed nothing. The executor then overruled Forge to attack P1 with Muldrotha into an untapped deathtouch Nazgûl, and she died. On P1's next turn Sauron, the Army and two Nazgûl hit us for 19 (30 to 7 counting drains). On our last turn we bounced only the Army token instead of the memo's three bounces, and P1's Sauron plus two Nazgûl dealt 18.
winnable_why: The table was rough. P2 drained its way to 60 life off Sephiroth and the emblem, and P1 kept rebuilding Wraiths behind a ward-protected Sauron. Even perfect play had to beat about 80 combined life. Still, the memos' Otawara-on-Sauron line (offered on four turns), a correct Deluge, and keeping Muldrotha home would have kept us in the game with Gray Merchant loops running. That is maybe a 15-25% game, not a likely win.

mistakes.what_happened: Round 9. After Toxic Deluge resolved at X=0, the executor overruled Forge's 'don't attack' and sent Muldrotha at P1, whose 2/3 deathtouch Nazgûl was untapped. Nazgûl blocked, and Muldrotha died (tax 2, so she cost 8 to recast). The round 8 memo had said not to attack and not to let deathtouch Wraiths fight Muldrotha.
mistakes.better_play: Keep Muldrotha home as a blocker. Once the Deluge had cleared nothing, she was the only thing between us and Sauron's army.
mistakes.why: Losing her removed our engine and our main blocker. P1's next swing did 19 and put us at 7.

mistakes.what_happened: Toxic Deluge was cast per the memo to wipe the Orc Army, Nazgûl and Sephiroth at X=5, which Muldrotha survives. X was Forge's choice and came out 0. Barrin (1/1), Gray Merchant, Nazgûl and Sephiroth all survived.
mistakes.why: Our one sweeper was spent for no effect, and P1's army stayed intact for the lethal swings.

mistakes.what_happened: The memos on turns 28, 32, 35 and 38 all planned to channel Otawara on Sauron and pay the ward by sacrificing Barrin. That costs {1}{U} with two legends out, isn't a spell (so no amass), and makes Sauron cost 8 to recast. It never happened. On turn 28 the spare mana went to cracking Mind Stone. On turn 32 it went to Gray Merchant instead of Otawara plus Apprentice. On turn 35 it went unused. The log doesn't show whether Forge offered the channel with the ward payment.
mistakes.better_play: Channel Otawara on Sauron on turn 28, while P1 was tapped out, then fire Ratchet Bomb as planned.
mistakes.why: Sauron's attacks dealt 7 per turn and every spell we cast grew P1's Army. Resetting him to the command zone at 8 mana was our best tempo play and the eventual cause of death.
mistakes.category: no removal on the real threat

mistakes.what_happened: At 7 life, facing a tapped Sauron 7/6, Army 7/7 and Nazgûl 6/7 and 5/6, the memo gave a survival line. Play Takenuma. Cast Mishra's Bauble. Barrin bounces the Army, sacrificing the Bauble. Otawara bounces the 6/7 Nazgûl. Barrin bounces the 5/6 Nazgûl, sacrificing an Island. Keep 2 open so that on P1's turn Gray Merchant blocks Sauron and Barrin bounces Merchant. The executor cast Bauble and made one Barrin bounce on the Army, which sacrificed an Island instead of the Bauble. It then cracked the Bauble to look at P1's library. No land drop was made, and Otawara and the second bounce never happened.
mistakes.better_play: Execute the memo line. P1 then attacks with Sauron alone into Merchant plus a bounce, and we take 0.
mistakes.why: The two Nazgûl we left dealt 11 of the 18 lethal damage.

mistakes.what_happened: Round 7. The executor overruled Forge's 'don't attack' to send Muldrotha at P1, leaving no untapped blocker. P1's crackback was Sauron 7 plus Gothmog 3. The executor also overruled Forge's no-block to chump the Army with Marionette Apprentice, which fed Sephiroth's emblem.
mistakes.better_play: Keep Muldrotha home, since an untapped 6/6 deters a Sauron swing, and take no chump blocks.
mistakes.why: It cost 10 life and a recursive drain piece, and the log shows no damage to P1 (still 25 on P1's turn).

strategy_assessment: The early plan was sound: Stormtamer, Apprentice, Baba, then Ratchet Bomb ticking for Ashnod's Altar and Sephiroth, then Muldrotha on round 6 with Stormtamer backup. It worked. Stormtamer countered Deadly Rollick, and the Bomb at 3 took out Altar, Sephiroth and later the Army. As in the other games, the memos treated P2's Sephiroth as the primary threat, but P1's Sauron was the real clock, and it needed answering on round 7. The strategist did see this: every memo from turn 28 on had Otawara on Sauron and a defensive posture. The failures were in execution and in Forge's X choice. The one strategist quibble is Gray Merchant held from round 4 to round 8 waiting for Muldrotha. An early Merchant for 3x3 drain plus 9 life, then recast later, would have cushioned the late drains.
summary: We lost to P1's Sauron and Nazgûl on round 10. The memos had the right answer, Otawara on Sauron with Barrin paying the ward, on four straight turns, and it was never executed. Then Forge cast our Toxic Deluge at X=0, and the executor attacked Muldrotha into an untapped deathtouch Nazgûl. P1's swings for 19 and 18 finished us. P2 at 60 life made this a hard table anyway.
